strings.name: Peter Norvig
strings.summary: Norvig connects AI research, search engineering and education. He co-authored Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach with Stuart Russell and led Google search and research teams and NASA Ames’s Computational Sciences Division; he now researches at Recursive and works in Stanford HAI education.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through AI textbooks, research on search technology and engineering practice, he has influenced computing education and large-scale intelligent systems.
strings.facts.f1.label: Raised in
strings.facts.f1.value: Rhode Island, Massachusetts and California, United States.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: B.S. in applied mathematics, Brown University; Ph.D. in computer science, University of California, Berkeley.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Organizing AI knowledge
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Russell, he brought search, reasoning, learning and decision-making into a coherent textbook framework, revised as the field developed.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Opening education to wider audiences
strings.highlights.h2.text: He co-taught a large online AI course with Sebastian Thrun and later advanced teaching centered on human needs, ethics and context.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Continuing human-centered AI teaching
strings.timeline.t1.text: His course directory lists Stanford CS139, extending teaching on design, social consequences and human goals.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Publishing Data Science in Context
strings.timeline.t2.text: With Alfred Spector, Chris Wiggins and Jeannette Wing, he examined foundations, application contexts and responsibility.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joining Stanford HAI
strings.timeline.t3.text: He became a Distinguished Education Fellow, developing tools and materials to explain central AI concepts.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-teaching an open online AI course
strings.timeline.t4.text: With Thrun, he opened a Stanford course worldwide, drawing over 100,000 registrations and supporting early MOOC development.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joining Google
strings.timeline.t5.text: He began at Google, later leading search-quality and research teams and contributing to machine learning and large information systems.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Leading NASA Ames computational sciences
strings.timeline.t6.text: His teams developed autonomous planning and related technology; the division’s Remote Agent experiment flew on Deep Space 1 in 1999.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-authoring an AI textbook
strings.timeline.t7.text: He and Russell published the first edition of Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, which became widely used in universities.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing his Brown degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned a B.S. in applied mathematics, then worked in software and pursued doctoral computer science research at Berkeley.
